newsitem.title: BRUNEI: Japanese PM arrives in Brunei in ASEAN tour start.
newsitem.headline: Japanese PM arrives in Brunei in ASEAN tour start.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto arrived here on Tuesday on the first leg of a five-nation Southeast Asian tour aimed at adding a political dimension to Tokyo's strong economic regional ties.
Hashimoto is scheduled on Tuesday night to hold a one-hour discussion on economic issues with Sultan Sir Hassanal Bolkiah, who is prime minister and absolute ruler of the tiny, oil-rich nation.

Japan is Brunei's largest trading partner as most of Brunei's liquefied natural gas and oil are exported to that country. In line with the sultan of Brunei's own efforts, Japan is keen to help the country diversify its oil-based economy.
"It is also hoped that the visit will contribute to diversifying the economy of Brunei," a statement from Japan's embassy in Kuala Lumpur said.
Hashimoto's visit to Brunei is his first to the sultanate, which shares the island of Borneo with the Malaysian states of Sabah and Sarawak and with Indonesia.
The last Japanese prime minister to visit Brunei was Kiichi Miyazawa in 1993.
Hashimoto's trip to five Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) members will take him next to Malaysia on Wednesday. He will also visit Singapore, Indonesia and Vietnam.
Japan's trade with the five nations stood at $74 billion in 1995, while its cumulative investment totalled $33 billion, Japanese foreign ministry figures said.
Hashimoto visited two other ASEAN members, Thailand and the Philippines, last year.

In recent years, Japan has intensified efforts to enhance its image in Brunei, diplomats said. "We do not want to be simply known as an exporter of cars and television sets," said a Japanese diplomat in Brunei prior to Hashimoto's arrival.
"Japan is looking for more human relations with South East Asian coutries," he added.
Hashimoto's Asia-Pacific strategy is expected to be underpinned by increasing economic cooperation with ASEAN countries and containing China's growing influence in the region.

The ASEAN tour had been in doubt because of the hostage standoff at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima. But Hashimoto said he would proceed with the visits as a sign of confidence in the Peruvian government's handling of the crisis.
